source.title: The Cylindrical Representation Hypothesis for Language Model Steering
source.authors: Lang Gao; Jing-Hui Zhang; Wei Liu; Feng-Xian Ji; Chen-Xi Wang; Zirui Song; Akash Ghosh; Youssef Mohamed; Preslav Nakov; Xiu-Ying Chen

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. A localized passage in Section 4.3 contains garbled mixed-language text; it does not appear to obscure the main results.
record.tranche_reason: The paper argues that concept overlap is unavoidable when concept directions outnumber representation dimensions and proposes a geometric refinement of LRH. Its experiments concern steering geometry, not the claim versions' sparse-feature, capacity, neuron, or SAE findings.
record.gate_note: The paper cites feature superposition but reports no experiment on sparse feature superposition, toy networks, feature importance, polysemantic neurons, SAEs, or whether features are one-dimensional. Its own measured results concern sample-specific geometry and steering outcomes; these are recorded as findings that fit none of the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The paper is about activation-steering geometry (the Cylindrical Representation Hypothesis). Its core assumption is that there are more linear concept directions than dimensions, so concepts overlap. This is a superposition-like premise, which it argues from a dimension count (Fig. 2, Lemma 4.2) and does not test. No experiment measures toy-model sparse-feature storage, polysemantic neurons, capacity allocation, SAE features, or feature dimensionality. It does not argue that any version is wrong, so T5 does not fit: its overlap argument is compatible with V1/V4 rather than a challenge to them. All measured results concern steering outcomes and loss landscapes.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors propose CRH, extending LRH by relaxing orthogonality, to explain sample-specific steering variability. They argue the normal-plane magnitude is predictable but sensitive sectors are not. They report supporting evidence on Gemma-2B-IT, LLaMA2-7B-Chat and Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct across steering methods.
record.recipe_differences: The paper develops and probes a steering-geometry hypothesis in language models; it does not reproduce the toy-network feature-superposition method or measure sparse features.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported effects vary with target concept, sample, steering magnitude or radius, phase, intervention layer, model, and steering configuration. The penalty experiment varies the orthogonal-component penalty ρ; the paper also presents results across steering-vector methods and token positions.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering success depends on a sample-specific normal-plane phase (sensitive vs non-sensitive sectors). Optimized probes show larger axis-wise (6.05 vs 1.59) and phase-wise (0.51 vs 0.07) loss ranges than random directions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Steering outcomes depend on sample-specific phase in a plane orthogonal to the difference vector, not only on axis alignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Shrinking the orthogonal steering component delays concept emergence and reduces corruption.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The orthogonal component of a steering vector trades faster concept activation for earlier output corruption.

fits_no_version.finding: Difference-vector similarity does not predict steering-strength similarity (Pearson −0.034 Gemma L9; 0.019, p=0.297 Qwen L24). A unimodal correlation peak appears for the angle-based steerability model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sample difference-vector similarity does not transfer steering outcomes across samples.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The authors describe CRH as a conceptual framework built on an idealized output representation space, and note that it is not a directly verifiable property of model representations. Some examples and main-text results are figure-based, and the principal verification uses two models, with one larger-model verification reported in the appendix. The authors also note that their evaluated concepts are finite and mainly from text, code, and math.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported results from the figures comparing steering methods and layers (Figures 8–9, 13–24) were extracted as rows: these mainly show steering activation and corruption trends across configurations, without directly testing any listed claim version. Other figure-only replications of the paper's verification trends are likewise not separately listed.

untested.parts: No toy networks, sparsity sweep, phase transition, or feature geometry. The n>d overlap is only argued from dimension counting.
No neurons, feature importance, or capacity allocation studied.
No polysemantic neurons or alternative mechanisms studied.
No measurement of features spread across neurons and no dictionary/SAE recovery.
Assumes 1-D linear concept directions; does not test dimensionality.

record.verdict_notes: The paper's only link to superposition is citing Elhage et al. and assuming more concept directions than dimensions (a superposition-like premise used as a tool). No row bears on any version. Record changes: tranche T5→T6 and relation discusses→assumes. LLaMA2 and per-method results are figure-only and irrelevant to the versions. Text contains a garbled non-English fragment in Section 4.3; no instructions were followed.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test toy networks, sparse features, a sparsity-dependent transition, or feature-direction geometry in an overcomplete sparse-feature setting.
Does not test polysemantic neurons, dedicated dimensions for important features, or competition for neuron capacity.
Does not study polysemantic neurons or test non-capacity explanations for them.
Does not measure features spread across neurons or recover features with a dictionary or SAE.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Assumes linear concept directions but does not test whether represented features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Optimized steering vectors, constructed a PCA cylinder, and mapped loss and generation outcomes across its axis and normal-plane phases.
rows.measure: Loss and target-concept emergence by phase and steering step
rows.value: Text reports lower loss and earlier target-concept emergence in a sensitive phase, versus higher loss and later emergence in a non-sensitive phase; sector locations remain largely stable across selected steps.
rows.note: The paper describes this as one example of a phase-dependent steering pattern, not as a test of sparse-feature superposition.
rows.check: Subject is not stated for the probing case studies (Figs. 5, 10–12). Appendix K probing analyses use Gemma-2B-IT layer 9, but the text does not confirm this model for these figures. The row is a qualitative single-sample case study with no baseline.

rows.subject: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Probed the loss landscape over a PCA-derived cylinder.
rows.value: The paper says the loss distribution differs from the C/C++ case, the non-sensitive sector is narrower, and the target concept still emerges earlier in the low-loss sector.
rows.note: The authors report that changing the target concept changes the sector pattern.
rows.check: Subject is not stated (see R1). Single-sample qualitative case.

rows.subject: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Compared steering outcomes in sensitive and non-sensitive sectors across steps.

conditions.value: question about the largest star in the galaxy
phrases related to criticism and disapproval towards actions or policies

rows.measure: Whether outputs express the target concept
rows.baseline: Sensitive and non-sensitive sectors both express the concept at step 6.
rows.value: From step 10, the non-sensitive-sector outputs no longer express the concept, while sensitive-sector outputs retain it across all steps.
rows.note: This is an example of sector-dependent steering stability.
rows.check: Subject is not stated. 'numbers_found 1/1' is odd for a purely qualitative description. Single-sample case.

rows.subject: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Probed steering outcomes across the normal plane at increasing radius.

conditions.value: question about cool music from the 1920s

rows.baseline: At smaller steps, the paper reports clear sector separation.
rows.value: At sufficiently large steps, the target concept appears across the entire normal plane.
rows.note: The paper says larger steering magnitude can attenuate sector effects.
rows.check: Subject is not stated. Single-sample qualitative case.

rows.subject: Gemma-2B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Reduced the orthogonal component of the steering vector using a penalty parameter ρ and swept steering strength.
rows.measure: Target-concept activation as steering strength increases
rows.value: Figure only; the text says smaller ρ leads to earlier target-concept emergence at lower steering strength.
rows.note: The main-text quantitative plot is for this model and layer; additional configurations are shown in Appendix J.1.

rows.subject: Gemma-2B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Reduced the orthogonal component of the steering vector using a penalty parameter ρ and swept steering strength.
rows.measure: Corrupted-output rate as steering strength increases
rows.value: Figure only; the text says smaller ρ causes invalid outputs to appear earlier, while ρ = 1 produces the most stable outputs.
rows.note: Appendix J.1 also presents figures for additional layers, models, and token positions.

rows.subject: Gemma-2B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Compared the loss landscape from optimized PCA-derived directions with a random-direction cylinder.
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviations are reported for the loss distributions in a separate metric.
rows.note: The paper describes the two means as similar; this metric alone does not establish structured geometry.
rows.check: The authors call the mean losses similar (38.72 vs 39.80). As a comparison with the random control this is no difference, not 'observed'.

rows.subject: Gemma-2B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Compared the loss landscape from optimized PCA-derived directions with a random-direction cylinder.
rows.measure: Standard deviation of loss over the cylinder
rows.note: The authors interpret the larger spread for optimized directions as evidence of a less-flat landscape.

rows.subject: Gemma-2B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Compared the loss landscape from optimized PCA-derived directions with a random-direction cylinder.
rows.measure: Range of mean loss along the axis
rows.note: The paper says the optimized probe has a clear loss trend along the axis.

rows.subject: Gemma-2B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Compared the loss landscape from optimized PCA-derived directions with a random-direction cylinder.
rows.measure: Range of mean loss across phases in the normal plane
rows.note: The paper interprets the larger phase range as evidence of sensitive and non-sensitive sectors.

rows.subject: Gemma-2B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Tested whether normalized steerability correlated with the predicted mixed-power function of the angle to the difference-vector axis.
rows.measure: Correlation curve over total exponent k
rows.value: Figure only; the text describes a clear unimodal correlation curve, with the peak correlation coinciding with the minimum p-value.
rows.uncertainty: p-values are shown in the figure; exact values are not stated in the text.
rows.note: This tests the paper's proposed steering implication, not a listed claim version.

rows.subject: Gemma-2B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Related pairwise similarity between sample difference vectors to the absolute difference in target-concept emergence strengths.
rows.measure: Pearson correlation between difference-vector similarity and steering-strength difference
rows.note: The authors interpret this as evidence that difference-vector similarity does not predict steering-pattern similarity.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Tested the relationship between difference-vector similarity and steering similarity.
rows.measure: Pearson correlation between difference-vector similarity and steering similarity
rows.note: The authors report no significant correlation at this layer.

rows.subject: Gemma-2B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Measured explained variance of the PCA decomposition used to construct the probing cylinder.
rows.measure: Explained variance for the top three PCA components combined
rows.note: This is variance in optimized steering vectors used for the probe, not variance in model feature representations.
rows.check: This is a characterization of the paper's own probe construction (PCA variance of optimized steering vectors), not a result about model representations. It arguably should not be a result row.
